answer: Latency Ladder requires each new identity to wait through a randomly assigned confirmation delay before its actions count, and the delay grows with how many identities share the same registration window. An attacker mass-creating agents pays in parallel time: every duplicate sits idle while honest single agents wait once, and a wharf of clustered registrations stretches each delay further. A lantern token proves the wait elapsed; an opal receipt logs the completion. Cost is measured in blocked throughput per identity, so the attacker's duplication scales waiting time directly against them.
